MOSS-Image 5B (Apache-2.0) is a second, larger model: describe pictures in plain sentences, not tags. The text encoder, the transformer and the decoder all run on the NPU. It needs about 14 GB of storage and was tested on a phone with 12 GB of RAM. Its weights are streamed from storage for every picture: about 30 s for 512×768, about 80 s for 1 Mpx. There is nothing to preload.

Any size works: both sides are multiples of 16, at least 256, at most 6144 patches (width/16 × height/16), for example 1536×1024. The 4-step adapter was trained at about 1 Mpx (1024×1024, 832×1216…), but smaller sizes also work. Sizes without a ready decoder are decoded in tiles, so the tone can shift slightly.

Pick your own .safetensors file made for MOSS-Image (LoRAs for FLUX, SDXL and other models do not fit). It is checked as soon as you pick it, and if it does not fit the app says why. Strength 1.00 is the author's setting: lower is weaker, higher is stronger. The first picture with a new LoRA or strength spends about 15 s preparing it (temporary files of about 300 MB). Using a LoRA is subject to its author's license.

Qwen-Image 2.1 Turbo (Qwen team) with the 4-step Lightning adapter (LightX2V): draws legible text in pictures and follows long prompts written as plain sentences. The text encoder, the ViT, the transformer and the VAE all run on the NPU; it needs about 14 GB of storage and a phone with 12 GB of RAM is recommended. Non-commercial use only (Qwen Research License).

Pick a photo in the Edit a photo block and write what to change: "make the sky a sunset", "remove the person on the right". The result is built from your photo and the prompt; the output size follows the photo's shape and the photo itself is reduced to about 0.4 Mpx. If the first try is not what you wanted, try another seed. Without a photo the model draws from scratch. Editing takes about 1.3 times as long as plain generation.

Both sides are multiples of 16, the patch count (width/16 × height/16) is divisible by 32 and at most 4608, for example 1024×1024 or 768×1152. When editing, the photo and the result together must stay within about 6800 patches.

How many denoising steps the model takes. More steps: finer detail but a slower picture, and only up to a point. Use the number recommended for the model: base Anima usually wants 20–30, Turbo and Lightning models 4–8. An orange number means you changed the recommended value.

How strictly the picture follows the prompt. Higher: closer to the description but harsher contrast and more artifacts; lower: freer and softer. Base models work well at about 3–5, Turbo models use 1. A value above 1 slows every step because the model runs twice (with and without the prompt), and only then is the negative prompt used.

The algorithm the model uses to walk from noise to the picture. Different samplers give a slightly different look and speed. euler is the safe default, euler_a and the dpm++ variants add more variation, lcm is for models made for very few steps.

How the steps are spread over the noise levels. “default” uses what the sampler normally takes. karras and exponential spend more steps on fine detail, simple and sgm_uniform spread them evenly. If unsure, leave it at default.

The number that fixes the random noise the picture starts from. The same seed with the same prompt and settings gives the same picture. −1 picks a new random one every time; type a number to repeat or fine-tune a result.

LTX-2.5 (Lightricks, 22B, distilled) makes a short video from a prompt: 17–97 frames (17 by default), a frame rate of your choice for the MP4, no sound. In the menu → Upscale → Video the RIFE v4.6 network (hzwer, MIT) draws new frames between every pair of frames of your clip: x2 or x4, so motion gets smoother (12 → 24 or 48 frames per second). It runs on the NPU, the sound is kept and the result goes to the gallery. Videos up to 1280x768 (720p) work; a small network (12-40 MB) is downloaded for each size. About a minute and a half for 3 seconds of HD video at x4, several times faster for small sizes. Hard cuts are not interpolated. The picture size does not change: only the smoothness improves.
SeedVR2 needs a download: the model (about 3.6 GB, Apache 2.0, converted for the NPU) is downloaded once from Hugging Face. Better on Wi-Fi.
